DESIGN SYSTEM (obey on EVERY slide so the deck is cohesive):
- Brand primary colour: #2563EB. Brand fonts: Noto Sans KR. Deck language: Korean.
- Canvas: a single 16:9 slide that renders at EXACTLY 1280x720px. Inline <style> only, no
  external JS. Body 1280x720, margin 0, overflow hidden.
- Document head: emit at most `<meta charset="utf-8">`. Never emit viewport, refresh,
  CSP, or any other meta `name`/`http-equiv` attributes; render security headers are
  injected by the application after validation.
- SELF-CONTAINED FONT POLICY: Never emit a Google Fonts <link>, CSS @import, remote font URL,
  @font-face, or data-font. Use a logical family plus its deterministic local fallback:
  "Noto Sans KR"/"Pretendard" -> "Malgun Gothic"; "Noto Serif KR" -> "Batang";
  "Inter"/"Roboto"/"DM Sans" -> "Aptos"; "Source Serif 4" -> "Cambria";
  "IBM Plex Mono" -> "Consolas". Example:
  `font-family:"Noto Sans KR","Malgun Gothic",sans-serif`.
  These rules make HTML render offline and editable PPTX typefaces deterministic. They do NOT
  mean that fonts are embedded in the PPTX; font embedding is outside this authoring workflow.
- Fonts: use the offline-safe logical stack "Noto Sans KR","Malgun Gothic",sans-serif; headings 800-900 weight, body
  400-500. Do not add any external font resource.
- Palette: build everything from the brand primary (#2563EB) + neutrals (ink #0F172A, muted
  #64748B, hairline #E2E8F0, surface #F8FAFC, white). The primary is the ONE accent; no other hues.
- SEMANTIC ROLES (the repair pass and the capacity gate read these marks):
  - Mark every text element with `data-semantic-role`, one of: title, body, supporting,
    decoration, image. Mark exactly ONE element per slide `data-semantic-role="title"` —
    the slide's title, on a cover the main title — on the element that directly contains
    that text, never `decoration`. `body` is the slide's readable content — sentences,
    bullets, descriptions, table text, card copy (most text owners on a content slide are
    `body`); `supporting` is short structural text only — sub-headings, eyebrows, labels,
    numbers with units, captions. A content slide must have body owners. Empty shapes and
    rules are `decoration`.
- SHARED UNIVERSALS (they hold whatever the style brief above says):
  - Margins ~64px on every edge, except an intentional full-bleed colour zone.
  - ONE accent hue per slide: the style's accent carries emphasis and everything else is
    ink, a neutral, or a tint of that accent. A second saturated hue is an error.
  - Eyebrow: UPPERCASE where the language has case, letter-spaced 0.15em, ~13px, in the
    accent, with a short tick or rule beside it.
  - Vary per slide (any of these, never all at once): full-bleed or partial colour-blocked
    zones, asymmetric grids, a left sidebar, oversized numerals, thin rules, and subtle
    tints of the accent.
- PPTX-NATIVE SAFETY (keeps exported objects editable):
  - Draw decorative ticks, underlines, badges, and divider lines as real <span>/<div> DOM
    elements, never ::before/::after pseudo-elements; painted pseudo-elements rasterize that subtree.
  - EXPLAIN THE SLIDE WITH STRUCTURE, NOT DECORATION: when the CONTENT states a process,
    a comparison, an architecture, a hierarchy, a schedule, or a set of figures, BUILD that
    relationship on the slide out of real DOM elements -- boxes, connector rules, lanes,
    columns, bars, rings -- carrying the CONTENT's own Korean labels and numbers. A page that
    restates its bullets as prose beside an ornamental picture has explained nothing. Prefer
    HTML+CSS (flex/grid, borders, gradients, box-shadow) for these: the converter maps DOM
    elements to native editable PowerPoint shapes, while an SVG is flattened to a bitmap.
    Tables, KPI figures, org charts, gantt bars and schedule rails, and simple 3-to-5 box
    process flows ALWAYS stay HTML+CSS DOM: a figure baked into a picture cannot be
    corrected, searched or re-used, so accuracy and editability outrank rendering ambition.
  - Do not use inline SVG for simple decoration; use HTML+CSS. Reserve SVG for geometry HTML
    genuinely cannot express -- curved or radial paths, polylines, arcs, wedges.
  - INLINE SVG CONTRACT (only when an essential chart or diagram truly needs SVG):
    - Root attributes: `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` (exact value, root only) plus
      `viewBox`, `width`, `height`, `preserveAspectRatio`; never `xmlns:xlink`.
    - Elements: only inert presentation shapes, text and paint definitions (g, path, rect,
      circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, text, tspan, defs, linearGradient,
      radialGradient, stop, clipPath, mask).
    - Attributes: only each element's ordinary coordinates plus transform, fill/stroke
      paint, opacity, dash, and text-metric attributes; paint may reference only a local
      fragment id such as `clip-path="url(#clip1)"`.
    - Never emit script, use, foreignObject, SVG image, animation, event attributes, href,
      xlink:href, or any network/file/data/javascript URL. Anything else is refused, and
      the rejection message names it.
  - Do not use text-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, or mix-blend-mode.
  - Use ONE radius family for the whole deck (one pixel value, applied uniformly). Per-corner
    radii are allowed only where the style itself names a tab or folder shape; export demotes
    that shape to raster, which is an acceptable price for it alone. No percentage radii.
  - Freely allowed: linear-gradient backgrounds, layered box-shadow, and raster images.
    Export keeps text, simple shapes and semantic tables as native editable PowerPoint
    objects and flattens whatever it cannot express — including a gradient field or a
    shadowed surface — into a picture BEHIND them. So use gradients and shadows for
    surfaces, and never to carry a value, a label, or the only cue that distinguishes
    two things.
- FORBIDDEN: default round bullet dots; identical heavy-shadow boxed cards on every item;
  clutter; lorem/placeholder; text overflowing/clipping the frame; low contrast; off-palette hues.
- FIT IS CRITICAL — the frame is EXACTLY 1280x720 and CLIPS (overflow:hidden): EVERY element
  must fit fully inside it with NO overflow, NO clipping, and NO overlap between blocks. This is
  the single most common failure — prioritise it over visual ambition. Use less/shorter text and
  generous spacing rather than cramming.
- NEVER hide overflowing content to make it "fit": `-webkit-line-clamp`, `line-clamp`,
  `text-overflow: ellipsis`, and `overflow`/`overflow-x`/`overflow-y: auto` or
  `scroll` are all forbidden and are rejected before rendering. If content does not fit, reduce
  density (shorter copy, fewer items) or re-lay out the slide instead — never truncate or make
  it scrollable.
- Width belongs to the CONTENT BOX, not the canvas: inside a container that is inset from the
  edge, an element is never 1280px wide. Subtract both insets (a 72px inset on each side leaves
  1136px) or set no width at all and let the container size it. Measured failures: three slides
  of one deck placed elements at x=72 with width:1280px, so each ran 72px past the right edge and
  clipped the source text inside it.
- The same arithmetic applies down the page: an element's top plus its height must stay above
  the footer safe zone. A block starting at y=749 on a 720px canvas is invisible, however
  correct its own box looks.
- TYPE SCALE: in ordinary authored generation and style-reference mode, set body copy, bullets,
  labels, and table cells at 18px or larger, and keep no visible content text (headings, body,
  bullets, tables, chart labels, metrics, callouts, captions, footnotes) below 13px (10pt
  equivalent). Express text sizes with `font-size` in px; do not use CSS `font` shorthand or
  relative units to evade this floor. Spare room on a slide goes into a larger type scale and
  more generous leading, not into one large empty band. If content does not fit, shorten it or
  allocate more space instead of shrinking it until it becomes unnecessarily hard to read.
- Heading sizing: size headings to the ACTUAL text length so they stay within their area, and
  budget vertical space for the real number of wrapped lines.
- No fragile positioning: never pin a TEXT block to a fixed top/absolute offset underneath a
  heading that could wrap to another line. Prefer normal document flow (flex/grid column with
  gaps) for content, and keep clear gaps between text blocks. Absolute positioning is for
  decorative layers, the page-number box, and the header contract's own band and body wrapper
  — those are fixed furniture and are meant to be pinned.
- Connector clearance: keep every line and its complete arrowhead bounding box inside a dedicated
  gutter, at least 12px away from text glyphs. Budget rotated arrowheads by their painted bounds,
  not only the unrotated CSS box; shorten the connector before reducing text clearance.
- Korean/CJK: set `word-break: keep-all` AND `overflow-wrap: break-word` on text containers so
  a Korean word is never split across lines and a single long token still cannot overflow its
  box. Set Hangul body copy to a line-height between 1.5 and 1.7 — Hangul needs more leading
  than Latin at the same size. Keep a numeral and its unit together on one line (one inline
  element around both, or a non-breaking space between them).
- Boxes/cards/labels: each one's text must fit ENTIRELY inside it with padding — never let text
  touch or clip an edge. Size the box to its content (or shrink the content to the box).
- SLIDE HEADER SYSTEM (decided once for THIS deck — reproduce it exactly on every slide):
  - This is the deck's single top-area design. Do not redesign, re-order, restyle, or 'improve' it per slide, and do not invent an alternative top treatment. Uniformity across slides outranks per-slide visual ambition.
  - Roles that skip the header entirely: COVER, SECTION. Those slides use their own composition and none of the rules below. They must also carry NO requirement identifier, badge, chip, or code anywhere on the slide, and must not imitate this header with an eyebrow-and-tick row of their own.
  - Header band: the top of the 1280x720 canvas, with 64px left and right margins. Its HEIGHT is not fixed for the deck: each slide DERIVES it from what that slide actually rendered, so a one-line title does not carry the space a two-line title needs. Everything else about the band is fixed and identical on every slide — two slides that render the same parts must come out at the same height, and the derived number is the only thing allowed to differ.
  - Left block = the eyebrow row (18px) + 12px + (number of title lines this slide actually renders x 45px).
  - Right block = 0. This deck's right slot is empty, so the band follows the left block alone.
  - Band height = 32px + max(left block, right block) + 28px, as a whole number of pixels, clamped to 96-280px. If the title would push it past the ceiling, SHORTEN THE TITLE — never shrink the type, never drop the gaps, and never exceed the ceiling.
  - Declare that number: the band root is <div data-header-part="band" data-header-band="N" style="height:Npx; ...">, where N is the same whole number in both places — a bare integer with no unit in the attribute, and an inline px height on that same element. The two must agree; a height that lives in a CSS class or is written in %, em, or calc() cannot be read back and counts as wrong. N is the band's whole rendered height, so put no padding or border on that element — or add box-sizing:border-box, which keeps them inside N. Space above the first row is already in the 32px the derivation starts from; spelling it again as padding makes the band taller than the number it declares.
  - Wrap ALL ordinary slide content in exactly one element marked data-header-part="body", and give that element an inline style saying where it starts: margin-top:20px when it follows the band in normal document flow, or position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:(N + 20)px when it is pinned — the full canvas width, matching how the band itself is pinned, because a position:absolute element with no left, right, or width has no horizontal extent and collapses to zero width, taking every child anchored inside it (e.g. left:0;right:0) down to zero width too. Use px in either form, and match the band: a band pinned with position:absolute takes up no room for a margin to follow, so its body must be pinned too or the whole header renders underneath the content. No slide content may enter the band, and the band's own parts stay outside this element.
  - Mark each part with its own data-header-part value: band, tick, eyebrow, title, subline, right, requirements, divider, body. Emit each marker at most once per slide and use no value outside that list. On the band's own parts use no data attribute other than data-header-part and data-header-band; attributes the slide is asked for elsewhere in this prompt are unaffected by this rule.
  - Accent tick: this deck has none. Never draw a rule, bar, or dot before the eyebrow.
  - Eyebrow: exactly one line of at most 24 characters, 13px, weight 700, letter-spacing 0.06em, colour #2563EB. It names this slide's own section — never the deck title, and never a separator-joined list of labels unless every slide of this deck uses that same form.
  - Eyebrow wording: Write it in Korean on EVERY slide of this deck — never in English or any other language, and never mixed. A deck whose eyebrow switches language between slides is wrong even if each slide reads well alone.
  - Title: 34px, weight 800, line-height 1.32, colour #0F172A, at most 2 line(s), maximum width 780px. Shorten the wording rather than shrinking the type or exceeding the line budget.
  - The line budget is a ceiling, never a target. A title that fits 780px is written on ONE line, and the band it derives is shorter for it — that room goes to the slide's content. Let a title reach a second line only when its own wording overflows the width, and never insert a manual line break to balance it, to split it at a phrase, or to make it look composed. Titles of the same deck are not expected to share a line count.
  - The title appears only inside the header band. Never repeat it below the band.
  - Subline: this deck has none. Never add a supporting line under the title inside the band.
  - Right slot: this deck leaves the right side of the band EMPTY. Never place a summary, label, badge, metric, logo, or icon there.
  - Requirement identifiers: this deck has none. Never render a requirement number, code, badge, or ticket reference in the band.
  - Divider: one real <div> of 1px filled #E2E8F0 at the bottom edge of the band, spanning x=64px to x=1216px.
- PAGE-NUMBER SYSTEM (ordinary authored generation and style-reference mode):
  - The COVER slide has no page number and no footer text.
  - Every slide after the cover has exactly one page-number text element in the precise bottom
    horizontal center. Use the per-slide PAGE MARKER instruction below as its only visible text.
  - Numbering starts at `01` on the slide immediately after the cover, increases by one on every
    following slide, and always uses two digits (`01`, `02`, `03`, ...).
  - Give that element a full-width fixed box (`position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:14px`),
    centered text, 12px type (9pt equivalent), 500 weight, 16px line-height, and #A7ACB3 color.
  - Reserve the bottom 72px as a footer safe zone (on a 1280x720 slide, all ordinary content must
    end at or above y=648px). Content, images, charts, tables, and decorative shapes must not
    overlap that zone or obscure the marker.
  - The footer contains the number only: never add `Page`, `페이지`, a slash/total, title,
    section name, wordmark, logo, or any other footer copy. Never place a page number at the top,
    in a corner, or anywhere else. Do not create a duplicate marker.
- All visible text in Korean.
Return ONLY the complete HTML document.
Capability contract: author the visual source only; do not claim editable Hybrid output. Native promotion is explicitly admitted later, and unsupported features are rasterized or rejected rather than silently downgraded.
DECK TOKENS (this deck's own values): ink #0F172A; accent #2563EB; accent-2 #2563EB; surface #F8FAFC; hairline #E2E8F0; radius 12px; gutter 24px; pad 28px; t-display 44px; t-h2 26px; t-body 18px; t-label 15px.
Use these exact values for colour, radius and spacing; any other hue is an error. Tints and shades of the ink and of the two accents are allowed, a new hue is not, and radius/gutter/pad are one family for the whole deck. Write the values literally in the CSS: do not declare CSS custom properties.
